subChunks.title: Strategy & Observer

storyBeats.text: Eldrin's combat system used to hardcode the attack algorithm. To change tactics in battle required stopping, rewriting, and redeploying. Strategy patterns changed everything.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Strategy encapsulates an algorithm and makes it interchangeable. The context class holds a reference to the strategy interface — not a concrete implementation. Swap strategies freely at runtime, test each in isolation, add new ones without touching the context.

storyBeats.label: Observer example

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Observer is the publish-subscribe model — a source emits events; all registered listeners receive them. The source knows nothing about its listeners; listeners know nothing about each other. This loose coupling is the core of event-driven architectures.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Implement Strategy: create a Greeter interface with greet(String name). Implement FormalGreeter (prints "Good day, [name]") and CasualGreeter (prints "Hey, [name]!"). Switch strategies and call both.
guidedPractice.hint: Use lambda expressions to implement both strategies inline.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the Strategy pattern. How does it relate to the Open/Closed principle?

questions.prompt: In the Observer pattern, what is the relationship between the subject and its observers?
options: Subject has a list of observers and notifies all when state changes
There is only one observer per subject
questions.answer: Subject has a list of observers and notifies all when state changes
questions.explanation: The subject (event source) maintains a list of observers and broadcasts state changes to all of them. This creates one-to-many loose coupling — the subject doesn't know the observers' concrete types.

subChunks.title: Command & Template Method

storyBeats.text: Eldrin creates a command crystal for every Academy action — each one can be cast, stored, and most importantly, reversed.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: The Command pattern turns actions into first-class objects. An object that can be stored, passed around, queued, logged, and undone. Every action in an undo-able editor, every transaction in a payment system — these are Commands.

storyBeats.label: Template method

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Template Method defines the skeleton of an algorithm and lets subclasses fill in specific steps. The skeleton is final — cannot be overridden. The variable steps are abstract. This is the Hollywood Principle: don't call us, we'll call you.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Implement a DataProcessor abstract class with a final process() template method that calls loadData(), transform(), and save(). Implement JSONProcessor with concrete versions of each.
guidedPractice.hint: The save() hook method has a default implementation. Only loadData() and transform() need to be overridden.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is the Command pattern used for? How does undo/redo functionality relate to this pattern?

questions.prompt: In the Template Method pattern, why is the template method typically declared final?
options: To prevent subclasses from changing the algorithm structure
To prevent it from being called
To allow it to call abstract methods
questions.answer: To prevent subclasses from changing the algorithm structure
questions.explanation: The template method defines the invariant algorithm skeleton. Making it final ensures subclasses can only override the variable steps, not the overall structure.
